statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is the earliest second in the following sense. For s with 1 <= s <= m, call s markable if there exist pairwise distinct seconds t_1,...,t_n in {1,...,s} and, for each i in {1,...,n}, a set D_i of exactly nums[i-1] distinct seconds contained in {1,...,t_i-1}, such that change_indices[t_i-1] = i for every i, and the sets D_1,...,D_n together with the singleton sets {t_1},...,{t_n} are pairwise disjoint. If some s in {1,...,m} is markable, r is the least such s; otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(change_indices). Assume 1 <= n <= 2000, 1 <= m <= 2000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and for every j with 0 <= j < m, 1 <= change_indices[j] <= n.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow occurs).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(change_indices). Assume 1 <= n <= 2000, 1 <= m <= 2000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and for every j with 0 <= j < m, 1 <= change_indices[j] <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= m.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(change_indices). Assume 1 <= n <= 2000, 1 <= m <= 2000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and for every j with 0 <= j < m, 1 <= change_indices[j] <= n.

statement: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(change_indices). For 1 <= s <= m, say s is markable iff there exist pairwise distinct seconds t_1,...,t_n in {1,...,s} and, for each i in {1,...,n}, a set D_i of exactly nums[i-1] distinct seconds contained in {1,...,t_i-1}, such that change_indices[t_i-1] = i for every i, and the sets D_1,...,D_n together with the singleton sets {t_1},...,{t_n} are pairwise disjoint. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, r is markable.

statement: Let ans(A) denote the value returned by the function on (A, change_indices), for any array A of length n with 0 <= A[i] <= 1000000000 for all i. For any two such arrays A and B, if A[i] <= B[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n, then ans(A) is no later than ans(B), treating -1 as +infinity: explicitly, if ans(B) != -1 then ans(A) != -1 and ans(A) <= ans(B), and if ans(B) = -1 there is no additional restriction.

statement: Fix any array A of length n with 0 <= A[i] <= 1000000000 for all i. Let ans(C) denote the value returned by the function on (A,C) for any nonempty list C of length at most 2000 whose entries lie in {1,...,n}. For any two such lists C and C' (both nonempty, length at most 2000, entries in {1,...,n}) such that C' extends C (len(C) <= len(C') and C'[j] = C[j] for every 0 <= j < len(C)), ans(C') is no later than ans(C) when -1 is treated as +infinity: explicitly, if ans(C) != -1 then ans(C') != -1 and ans(C') <= ans(C), and if ans(C) = -1 there is no additional restriction.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, for each index i in {1,...,n} let p_i be the last second in {1,...,r} with change_indices[p_i-1] = i. Order the indices as i_1,...,i_n so that p_{i_1} < p_{i_2} < ... < p_{i_n}. Then for every k with 1 <= k <= n, sum_{h=1}^{k} (nums[i_h-1] + 1) <= p_{i_k}.
